title: Hoist loop-invariant assumptions out of loop headers
motivation: A `while` loop's header ends in a checkpoint, so a type assumption such as `n ?: v1(R)` and the `unbox` that follows it ran on every trip, although `n` is defined outside the loop and never changes. In C each trip paid the checkpoint branch with the inline type test, the `PROTECT`/`UNPROTECT` of the assumption result, and the `unbox` load. empty_while, scalar-while, bytecodes, sieve and vector_while showed this cost.
solution: The new pass `HoistLoopAssume` handles a loop whose header has no statement, ends in a checkpoint, and has one entry edge from outside the loop. It moves the leading `?:`, `?-` and `?=` assumptions on registers that are defined outside the loop and are not owned or fresh to a new checkpoint on that entry edge. The new deopt block is a copy of the header's deopt block, with each header phi replaced by its argument on the entry edge, so a failure leaves the frame of the first trip. `ElideUnusedCheckpoints` then removes the header checkpoint if no assumption stays, and `Optimizations` runs the pass just before `MergeConsecutiveCheckpoints`.

files.server/src/main/java/org/prlprg/fir/opt/: New pass that moves a loop header checkpoint's invariant assumptions to a new checkpoint, with a copied deopt block, on the loop's entry edge.
Runs `HoistLoopAssume` before `MergeConsecutiveCheckpoints` and `ElideUnusedCheckpoints` when checkpoints may change.
